items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: I remember Sharky going to New York in 1936 1936 and 37 when I first heard Brunus in 1936 I believe he was playing with Sharky

ctx.x: they might not have all been working with Lou at that particular early period 1938 but Lou was getting little bands together so they were having Dixieland their so-called whatever you'd say out there I don't know I never did see it really die out like in Chicago Johnny Dodds and Baby Dodds all those fellas were working all the time and they made all those records like for Decca that session Louis Armstrong in a way had a sort of usually a big band but I mean he was playing some New Orleans music all the time and…

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: Sharky's band was up there at Nick's at about 1936

ctx.x: and was it Jasmine that started an interest again in New Orleans music or was it the so called Dixieland revival as it's popularly called with the issuing of some of the mostly records of people like Bunk Johnson

oh I don't know there was it's hard for me to say exactly there had been a lot of interest in New York in the type of music Sharky's band was up there at Nick's at about 1936 and of course Nick used a lot of the New Orleans people along with the Eddie Condon people people like Zutty and Boucher was there they would sometimes be in a different group Boucher for instance worked in the group called Spirits of Rhythm which he didn't like especially one thing they used electric guitars and he remember one night…
